title: Never-look entries cover window titles again, and the ask box's context keeps what was focused and selected
owns: app/main/perception/elements.ts and the never-look matching, app/main/ask-open.ts and the ask context read (Focused:, Selected text:), app/main/perception quick context

items.title: A never-look entry the user typed that equals "keeper", "seahorse" or "strongbox" no longer covers window titles (for example the Keeper web vault in a browser)
items.scenario: Review #120 made the defaults that are everyday words match the window's app only. isNeverLook applies that rule to any list entry that folds to one of those words, including ones the user typed. Settings says 'Ember never reads, captures or acts in an app or window whose name contains one of these', and the commit message (bb81ff2) says 'the user's own entries ... match the app or the title as before'. Example: on Linux or macOS, where "keeper" isn't a default, a user adds "Keeper" to keep Ember out of the Keeper web vault in Firefox. The window "My Vault | Keeper - Mozilla Firefox" is still read and acted in, and the policy allows the read. On Windows, the default "keeper" also stopped covering Keeper's web vault in Edge, while "bitwarden" still covers Bitwarden's web vault by title. The existing unit test notes the list can't tell a user's entry from a default, but the UI promises title matching.
items.evidence: I reproduced it with a scratch test, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/relfix3-review/safety/tree/test/unit/zz-safety-neverlook.test.ts. Output: `SCRATCH isNeverLook(user Keeper): false`, `SCRATCH read decision: allow reading is allowed`, `SCRATCH isNeverLook(user 'Keeper Vault'): true`, `SCRATCH win default keeper/Edge: false`, `SCRATCH win default bitwarden/Edge: true`. The code is elements.ts isNeverLook: `return !!i && (NEVER_LOOK_APP_ONLY.has(i) ? app.includes(i) : hay.includes(i));`, applied to every list item, and the sidecars mirror it (sidecar-host/windows.ts neverLooked, desktop-child.ts).
items.fix: Apply the app-only rule only to defaults. Either store defaults distinctly (for example mark them when Restore defaults or a fresh install writes them), or match those words against titles as whole words, so a typed "Keeper" still covers "... | Keeper - Firefox". Alternatively, say in settings that these three words match the app only, and let the user add a title-matching entry.

items.title: On Windows (and likely macOS) the ask box now always has the keyboard before the quick context is read, so 'Focused:' and 'Selected text:' drop out of the ask context
items.scenario: Windows: the user selects a sentence in Word or Notepad and presses Win+Alt+Space, then types 'make this bold'. openAsk takes the user's window (userWindowsNow, main.ts:1012), then openAskInOrder calls show() before read(active) (ask-open.ts:36-37). show() runs reveal() synchronously: win.show(), win.focus() and takeFocus, which on Windows calls inputRef.activate(id) and focusInput(id) (main.ts:914-918). Only after that does the readWindow request go to the host. The host's UIA walk reads HasKeyboardFocus, which is system-wide keyboard focus and is false for every element of the user's window once the box is foreground. With no focused node, the host asks no element for its selection, and quickContextText writes neither the 'Focused:' line nor 'Selected text:'. Windows has no PRIMARY-selection fallback (platform.clipboard is null on win32 and darwin). The request's context therefore names only the app and window, not what 'this' is. macOS's AXFocused probably behaves the same once the non-activating panel is key; I did not verify that on a real Mac.
items.evidence: ask-open.ts:28-38: `o.show(); o.read(active);` when an active window was taken (always on Windows and macOS, since keyboardHold is null there). main.ts:914-918: takeFocus calls `inputRef?.activate(id); inputRef?.focusInput?.(id)` inside reveal(), i.e. before read(). app/sidecar-host/providers/uia.ts:142: `set("focused", b.hasKeyboardFocus)`. app/sidecar-host/tree.ts:188-215: `wants.selection` is set only `if (focused)`. app/main/perception/index.ts:913-923: quickContextText takes focus and selection only from focusedElement(seen.nodes). win32/platform.ts:70 and darwin/platform.ts:58: `clipboard: null`, so Perception.withSelection adds nothing. At 9912de5, captureContext() was dispatched before askWindow.show(), so this was already a race that the walk often lost on Windows. typeahead2 makes the loss certain. No integration test checks quickContext on any OS (grep for quickContext / 'Selected text' under test/integration finds nothing). The worker can still re-read the screen once the box closes, so nothing becomes unusable; the initial context and the box's 'Ember will see' line lose the selection.
items.fix: Before show() on Windows and macOS, take the focused element and its selection cheaply. For example, have userWindowsNow also ask the host or input layer for the focused element (UIA FocusedElement with its TextPattern selection, or AX AXFocusedUIElement with AXSelectedText) and pass it into quickContext. Alternatively, have the read in quickContext take the window's last-focused element (UIA: the element whose hwnd is the window's GUI-thread focus; AX: the app's AXFocusedUIElement, which survives deactivation) instead of the per-node HasKeyboardFocus/AXFocused state. Add an ember-win32 integration check that a selection made in the bench before the ask chord shows up in the ask context.
